ai.description: The Badakhshana Rock Agama reaches 12 cm in snout-vent length. It is grey-brown with a dark-spotted back and a bright yellow or orange throat. Distinctive features include a flattened body and tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Paralaudakia badakhshana* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, enlarged, and fan-shaped cluster of spinose scales on the sides of the neck.
ai.habitat: *Paralaudakia badakhshana* inhabits high-altitude rocky slopes and boulder-strewn terrain in the Hindu Kush, typically found between 2,000 and 3,500 meters in arid zones.
ai.behavior: The Badakhshana rock agama is a diurnal lizard that actively basks on rocky outcrops to regulate its body temperature before foraging for small insects and plant matter.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Paralaudakia badakhshana* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 3–6 eggs. Breeding occurs during the spring and summer months.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Paralaudakia badakhshana* is found in the high-altitude regions of the Hindu Kush in northern Pakistan and adjacent areas, typically occurring above 2,000 meters.
